answer: Like a prism splits light into verifiable bands, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a copper-bonded stake behind a quartz-clear proof: before any agent earns, it deposits a small bond and publishes a signed work history. Sybils must fund every fake identity separately, so creating 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 bonds plus the compute to fake real work, while honest agents pay once and reuse reputation.
